chapter: The Latin scene and business of the 1940s-70s
title: La Conga's audience and the second band
summary: His audience was largely Jewish; Corbello played second band.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: When you were playing in the Conga, you played in La Conga for what, three years?
Yeah, but that --
What was your public?
Public? Ninety-five percent were __________. They were the first people who took (inaudible).
And you were playing -- your second band was __________, right?
No, no, no, no, I (inaudible).
Right.
I brought __________ there to play second bass for me.
That's what I say, yeah.
I was the main band there.
Sure.
When I got there, Jahari got his own
band there, American .
Right. And so you had to take Corvello as second --
And then, after I stayed there about five, six months (unintelligible). And then I would bring Corvello there to play the -- when I finish with my show, I said, Corvello, keep on playing Cuban music.
Right.
Because that used to start playing that music with his band, and the people used to leave the club.
Was that the Corvello band with Tito Rodriquez singing? Or did that come --

No, no, no, no, no. Corvello hired first -- he hired -- had about two or three different guys. He had Paulo Flore, he had Polito Golindez, he had -- another kid I recommended, I forgot his name, I never seen him no more, and then after that, Corvello got hold of (unintelligible) and Bobby Scott. And that's when he got his best band.
And when you say you had a Jewish public, but was the Conga a club that attracted a kind of a carriage trade or --
Well, the average people that went there, they went there -- all these people in the fur business, all the people in the business.
How much did it cost to get into the Congo Room?
Well, nothing.
You were free to get in?
You were free to go (unintelligible), charge a minimum charge, whatever it was. It was no dance hall, we'd charge admission (unintelligible).
